figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Effects of EG on HMGB1 release and TLR4 expression. (A) HUVEC monolayers were pretreated with the indicated concentrations of EG for 6 h and then stimulated with
LPS 100 ng/ml for 16 h. HMGB1 release was then measured by ELISA. (B) Male C57BL/6 mice underwent CLP and were administered EG intravenously 12 h later (n = 5). Mice
were euthanized 24 h after CLP. Serum HMGB1 levels were measured by ELISA. C, Conﬂuent HUVECs were incubated with LPS (100 ng/ml, C) for 3 h with or without EG pre-
treatment for 6 h. Lycopene (20 lM, Lyc) was pre-treated for 6 h as a positive control. The expression of TLR4 on HUVECs was measured by cell-based ELISA. (D) The effects of
EG on cellular viability were determined using an MTT assay. Results are means ± SDs of three different experiments. ⁄p < 0.05 or ⁄⁄p < 0.01 vs. LPS (A and C) or CLP (B).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Effects of EG on vascular barrier permeability in vitro and in vivo. The effects of various concentrations of EG on LPS (A, 100 ng/ml) or HMGB1 (B, 1 lg/ml)-mediated
barrier disruption were monitored by measuring the ﬂux of Evans blue bound albumin across HUVECs in a transwell chamber. (C) The effects of EG (4.5 mg/mouse or 9.0 mg/
mouse, i.v.) on HMGB1-induced (2 lg/mouse, i.v.) vascular permeability in mice were also examined by measuring the ﬂux of Evans blue into the peritoneal cavity in mice
(expressed lg/mouse, n = 5). Results are expressed as means ± SDs of three separate experiments. ⁄p < 0.05 or ⁄⁄p < 0.01 vs. LPS (A) or HMGB1 (B, C).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. Effect of EG on F-actin rearrangement. Staining for F-actin. HUVEC monolayers grown on glass coverslips were stimulated with HMGB1 for 1 h and then
immunostained for F-actin. Arrows depict intercellular gaps. The results shown are representative of three independent experiments.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Effects of EG on HMGB1-mediated pro-inﬂammatory responses. (A) The HMGB1 (1 lg/ml)-mediated expressions of VCAM-1(white box), ICAM-1 (gray box) and E-
selectin (black box) in HUVECs were analyzed after treating monolayers with the indicated concentrations of EG for 6 h. (B) HMGB1 (1 lg/ml)-mediated adherence of
leukocytes to HUVEC monolayers was analyzed after treating cells with the indicated concentrations of EG for 6 h. (C) HMGB1 (1 lg/ml for 16 h)-mediated migration of
leukocytes through HUVEC monolayers was analyzed after treating cells with the indicated concentrations of EG for 6 h. (D) HMGB1 (2 lg/mouse, i.v.)-mediated migration of
leukocytes into peritoneal cavities was analyzed after treating mice with 4.5 or 9.0 mg/mouse (i.v.) and the values was expressed x 106, (n = 5). Results are expressed as the
means ± SDs of three experiments. ⁄p < 0.05 or ⁄⁄p < 0.01 vs. HMGB1 alone.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. Effects of EG on HMGB1-induced NF-jB activation and on TNF-a production in HUVECs. (A) The HMGB1 (1 lg/ml)-mediated activation of phospho-NF-jB p65 in
HUVECs was analyzed after treating cells with EG. (C) HMGB1 (1 lg/ml)-mediated TNF-a production was analyzed after treating cells with EG. (B and D) Male C57BL/6 mice
were administered EG intravenously at 12 h after CLP (n = 5). Mice were euthanized 24 h after CLP. Levels of activated phospho-NF-jB p65 (B) and TNF-a (D) in serum were
analyzed. Results are expressed as the means ± SDs of different three experiments. ⁄p < 0.05 or ⁄⁄p < 0.01 vs. HMGB1 alone.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 7. Effect of EG on mortality after CLP. (A) Male C57BL/6 mice (n = 10) were administered EG at 4.5 lg/mouse i.v. (h) or at 9.0 lg/mouse i.v. (j)12 h after CLP. (B) Mice
were administered EG at 4.5 lg/mouse i.v. (h) or at 9.0 lg/mouse i.v. (j) at 12 or 50 h after CLP. Animal survival was monitored 6 hourly for 128 h after CLP. Control CLP mice
(d) and sham-operated mice (s) were administered sterile saline (n = 10). Kaplan–Meier survival analysis was used to evaluate overall survival as compared with CLP mice.
